question:
A nucleus X has mass number $A=20$ and atomic number $Z=10$. Its binding energy per nucleon is measured to be $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)=8.03\,\text{MeV}$.

Given: $m_H=1.007825\,u$, $m_n=1.008665\,u$, $1\,u\,c^2=931.5\,\text{MeV}$, and atomic mass of $^4\!He$ is $M(^4\!He)=4.002603\,u$.

(a) Calculate the total binding energy $BE_X$ of nucleus X.

(b) Using mass–energy equivalence, determine the mass defect $\Delta m_X$ (in $u$) and hence compute the atomic mass $M_X$ using
\ $M_X = Zm_H+(A-Z)m_n-\frac{BE_X}{931.5}$ 

(c) Compute the binding energy of one $^4\!He$ nucleus from the given atomic mass data and hence find the total binding energy of $5$ alpha particles.

(d) Evaluate whether the breakup $X \rightarrow 5\alpha$ is energetically possible without external energy by calculating the $Q$-value using binding energies.

options.A: $M_X\approx 19.9925\,u$; $\Delta m_X\approx 0.172\,u$; $Q\approx -19.1\,\text{MeV}$ so breakup into $5\alpha$ requires energy input
options.B: $M_X\approx 20.172\,u$; $\Delta m_X\approx 0.172\,u$; $Q\approx +19.1\,\text{MeV}$ so breakup into $5\alpha$ is spontaneous
